extracted.intended_audience: chemical patent searchers, indexers, and DWPI/Dervent users (information specialists performing chemical/Markush searches)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and indexing rules for selecting and using the BCE Chemical Fragmentation Codes to index and search chemical patents in Derwent World Patents Index (DWPI). Covers code structure, applicability, priority rules, special-purpose codes, polymer/halogen conventions, and use of Markush TOPFRAG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical Codes represent structure fragments and related descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: The BCE Chemical Codes are a set of alphanumeric symbols, each of which represents a chemical structure fragment, a biological activity, a formulation, a use, or a property disclosed in a patent document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: F431 represents a pyridine ring. Codes are used to index patents classified in Derwent Sections B (pharmaceutical), C (agricultural), and E (general chemical).

rubrics_metrics.name: BCE applicability (Sections B, C, E)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chemical Codes are used to search for patents in CPI Sections B, C, and E (sometimes referred to as the 'BCE Chemical Codes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes them from Section A (Plasdoc) polymer codes and from DWPIM variable-structure searching; users should confirm that the patent's CPI section is one of B, C, or E before relying on BCE codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical Codes divided into Parts A–W
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chemical Codes are divided into 21 categories (Parts A: through W:) that group related code types (e.g., Elements Present, Ring Systems, Functional Groups, Miscellaneous, Reactions, Activities/Uses, Formulations, Steroids, Polymers, Dyes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should consult the relevant Part for the kind of feature being coded (e.g., rings in D–G, functional groups in H/J/K/L, miscellaneous/linkages in M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-character code hierarchy and truncation
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal four-character Chemical Codes are hierarchical: first character = Part, first two = Set, first three = Subset, four characters = specific code. A colon (:) truncation symbol represents further characters and allows searching of whole Sets/Subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truncation enables searching an entire Set (truncate after second character) or Subset (truncate after third character). Example hierarchy: Part H:, Set H7:, Subset H73:, Code H7301 ('C(C) Present in a Ring').

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-purpose codes: negation, Poly, control, precursor
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-character negation (essential) codes are used for negative searching (indicating functional groups present/absent). Poly codes (four-character) indicate that one of a group of codes is applicable more than once. Control codes in Set M9: direct searches to designated portions of the database. Precursor (discontinued generic) codes represent older, less-specific codes replaced by more specific ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negation codes are primarily used with functional groups (see functional groups chapter). Poly codes do not mean that multiple different codes apply, only that a member of the group applies more than once. Precursor codes must be considered for retrieval of pre-1981 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle precursor codes and 1981 code modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A # sign indicates that a newer code replaced an older less-specific code (precursor). Precursor codes (created by replacing final digit with '0') should be OR'ed with newer codes to retrieve earlier references indexed under the old code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If precursor codes are omitted, retrieval of pre-1981 references will be less specific or incomplete. Some older codes were split into two new codes; older references indexed under the older code will be retrieved by either new code, potentially increasing irrelevant hits for pre-1981 documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Markush TOPFRAG but verify results
rubrics_metrics.description: Markush TOPFRAG automatically converts a user-drawn (topological) chemical structure into a Chemical Code search strategy, including free sites and Markush variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic strategies are helpful for newcomers, but can be too precise or otherwise not match the user's intent; users should look up definitions of codes generated by TOPFRAG in the manual and adjust (delete or add codes) to improve relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select applicable codes by structure analysis (mapping to Parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: First step in strategy development is to analyse the structure and divide it into 'codeable' fragments; different fragment types map to specific Parts: inorganic compounds/ions/ligands to Parts A/B/C; elements other than H,C,N,O,S to A/B/C; ring systems to D/E/F/G; number of ring systems to Set M5:; functional groups to B/H/J/K/L; carbon chains/ring-to-ring linkages to Part M:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most common elements (H,C,N,O,S) are only indexed as individual elements for inorganic compounds; otherwise they are indexed via the rings and functional groups. Use this mapping to find candidate codes for each fragment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous ring codes: use Ring Index Numbers (RINs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ring codes ambiguously cover more than one ring system; RINs (Ring Index Numbers) can be added to the search strategy to make retrieval more precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An asterisk (*) next to a ring code indicates RINs have been assigned. Consult the RIN listings when a ring code could represent multiple structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand rules and restrictions at all hierarchy levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicability of codes is governed by introductions, notes, and rules at Part, Set, Subset, and individual code levels; these must be understood before using a code in a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to read hierarchy-level notes can cause searches to behave unexpectedly. Always consult the rule text at every level relevant to a selected code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope vs definition — a code may match structurally but be inapplicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a code's short definition appears to match a fragment, the overall scope of applicability may exclude the compound type in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a trivalent N in a pyridine ring might seem to match a C107 code, but Part C: codes are for inorganic compounds—pyridine should be coded by ring code F431 instead. Always consult scope statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadings and Derwent Section restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each code can only be used with certain subheadings (based on compound type) and some codes are only assigned to patents classified in specific Derwent Sections (e.g., most Part R: codes only for Section B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check subheading applicability (M1, M2, M4, etc.) and Section restrictions when selecting codes for indexing or search construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rules for functional groups and ethers
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple functional-group codes could apply, priority rules determine which code is assigned: for functional groups, consult Part K: first, then Part L:, Part H:, and finally Part J:. For ethers, only the highest-priority ether attachment is coded in the order heterocyclic > aromatic > alicyclic > aliphatic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if an ether oxygen is bonded to one alicyclic ring and one heterocyclic ring, code only the 'Ether bonded to heterocyclic carbon' and not the alicyclic attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rule: only first correct code in a Set/Subset is assigned
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Sets/Subsets follow the rule that only the first correct code in that Set or Subset is assigned; other equally correct codes in the same Set/Subset are ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Set M4: (type of compound) lists codes M411–M417; if 'inorganic' is the first applicable term, it is the only one added even if other fragment types exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred structural forms and tautomer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes are assigned to preferred structural forms according to coding rules (e.g., keto-enol tautomerism: code the keto form unless the enol -OH is bonded to a fully conjugated carbocyclic ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous rules apply to thioxo-thiol tautomers and other tautomeric systems. Preferred forms of dyestuffs are listed in the dyes chapter; follow these conventions when choosing codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding sheet is a summary memory device only
rubrics_metrics.description: The coding sheet gives only an abbreviated summary of each code and should be used as a memory device or to find potentially applicable Sets, not as a complete coding guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always consult the detailed user guide text for rules and examples before finalizing a code selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polymer coding rules (addition vs non-addition; pre/post-1981)
rubrics_metrics.description: Polymers have special polymer codes; Section B polymers receive Part V: codes. Hypothetical monomers of >C=C< addition polymers are assigned all applicable Chemical Codes. Prior to 1981, non-addition polymer monomers/condensants were structure-coded; from 1981 forward, many non-addition polymers are coded as single compounds (monomers not individually coded), with Poly codes indicating repeated groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 1981 forward, negation codes and M1/M2/M3 codes are assigned to polymers/polypeptides; consult your local Derwent office for extensive polymer indexing resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halogen coding rules and mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: The code Part(s) used for a halogen-containing group depend on the atom(s) to which the halogen is bonded. The halogen atom itself is identified in Set C0: or Subset H60:, depending on bonding context; functional groups formed with the halogen may receive further codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide provides a list of mapping cases: (1) halogen bonded to metal use C0:, A940; (2) halogen anion C0:, C720; (3) halogen in inorganic/ion/ligand C0:; (4) monovalent halogen bonded to C (but not to C=U) H6:; (5) halogen bonded to heteroatoms use specified K/L codes; (6) valency of halogen use L760,C100,C200,C300; (7) halogen as ring member C600,C0:; (8) halogen bonded to C=U use L330,L353,L511,L512. Check subset notes for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable/unknown substituents: OR together applicable codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Variable substituents are represented in Chemical Code searches by OR'ing together codes for the possible substituents; related affected codes must also be OR'ed if they change depending on substituent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can increase complexity of the search strategy; weigh the trade-off between specificity and manageability. Ensure all variable possibilities are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify compound's role is significant before coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Before selecting codes, the user should verify whether the role the searched compound is likely to play in patents of interest is significant enough that Derwent would code it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Selecting the Compounds to be Coded' (page 27). Not all compounds mentioned in a patent are coded—only those considered significant for indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of pre-1981 versus post-1981 coding on retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Many coding changes occurred in 1981 (Derwent Week 27). Some older codes were converted one-to-one, others split into more specific codes or replaced by groups of newer codes; older references may be indexed under precursor codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing searches across time ranges, OR precursor codes with newer ones to ensure complete retrieval or be aware that older references may be less specifically indexed, producing more irrelevant hits when matched to newer codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and use of Poly codes
rubrics_metrics.description: A Poly code located at the end of many Sets/Subsets indicates that one of the coded group is applicable more than once to a structure; Poly does not mean multiple different codes apply simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poly codes are not provided in Sets/Subsets whose codes specify an exact number of occurrences. Use Poly codes to represent multiplicity of a feature rather than multiple distinct features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation codes for negative searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-character negation (essential) codes are designed for negative searching and the removal of irrelevant references; they mainly indicate functional groups that are present or absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negation codes are discussed in detail in the chapter on functional groups and are particularly useful for excluding unwanted structural variants from search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypeptide/amino-acid coding thresholds and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set V9: and related rules govern coding of polypeptides: amino-acid chains of 1–3 units are indexed as non-polymeric compounds and structure-coded in Parts D–M; from 1981 forward, a 3-unit amino acid chain also receives applicable Part V: codes in subfield M2. Chains of 4 or more alpha amino acids are indexed as polypeptides; structure codes for individual amino-acid units are listed under subheading M1, but amide linkages are not coded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set V9: codes are not used for dipeptides. From 1981 forward negation codes from H–L have been assigned to polypeptides (applied to the polypeptide as a whole, excluding amide linkages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dye coding conventions and preferred forms (Part W:)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part W: codes are assigned to organic colouring compounds (dyes, pigments, immediate precursors, fluorescent brighteners). Conventions specify preferred coded forms: e.g., keto-hydrazone dyes coded as azo-phenol, quinone-diazide precursors coded as diazonium-phenoxide, tri-aryl methane dyes as carbonium, phthalein/xanthene coded ring-open while their precursors ring-closed, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate precursors of dyes/pigments receive Part W: plus Q317 or Q318. Ionic cyanine dyes assume charge placement rules that affect hydrogenation and ring coding. Metal-complex dyes are coded in separate subfields for each dye-metal or metal-non-dye fragment. Natural dyes of unknown structure additionally receive V792 and M423. Conventional non-essential counter ions are not coded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part W: subheading applicability and code usage notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, Part W: codes are applicable to Subheading M4 from the beginning of the service (1970). W00–W05 etc. have specific notes: e.g., W002 for metallised dyes (metal chelate rings), W003 for non-metallised dyes, W004/W005 for dye residue/general when insufficient info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Part W: notes for when to use generic dye descriptors (W001–W005) vs specific dye-type codes and for how to combine dye codes with other Parts and subheadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use code subfields for metal-complex dyes
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes for metal-complex dyes are divided into different code subfields based on dye structure: (dye1)-metal-(dye2) is coded with (dye1)-metal codes in one field and metal-(dye2) codes in another; likewise for (dye)-metal-(non-dye).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separation ensures accurate representation of complexed parts and supports searching on either side of the metal complex independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control codes in Set M9: and time-range control
rubrics_metrics.description: Control codes in Set M9: direct the search strategy to only examine designated portions of the DWPI database; time-range control codes are available to limit searches to specific coding eras or service dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use M9 control codes when you need to restrict retrieval to particular segments (e.g., pre/post-1981 indexing) or known database subsets; detailed discussion begins on page 22 of the guide.
